metadata.theme: Courage, noticing small details, and asking for help
metadata.premise: When thick fog swallows the harbour, young lamp keeper Fen must find out why the old lighthouse lamp went dark before the fishing boats come home.

items.name: Soft cloth
items.description: A soft cloth from the old chest. It is made for wiping the brass mirror.

items.name: Match tin
items.description: A small tin of long matches from Gran Tull. They will light the wick.

clues.name: Damp mirror
clues.description: Fog leaves wet mist on the brass mirror. A misty mirror makes a dim lamp.

passages.title: The Fog Rolls In
paragraphs: Fen stood on the path by the old lighthouse. The fog was thick and grey.
The lamp at the top was dark. Out at sea, every ship and fishing boat needed that light.
Gran Tull, the old lamp keeper, sat on the bench by the tower door. She wore a thick wool coat.
Pip the gull hopped onto the bench. Pip tapped a shell with her beak, tap, tap, tap.
Fen felt a bit afraid. But Fen wanted to help much more.

choices.label: Look in the shed for a lamp tool
Sit on the bench and ask Gran Tull

passages.title: The Garden Shed
paragraphs: The shed door was shut. Fen lifted the chain and pushed.
The door creaked wide. Inside, fish nets hung from the wall.
An old chest sat under the shelf. A dry shell lay on the lid.

passages.title: Inside the Chest
paragraphs: Fen lifted the lid of the chest. A grey moth fluttered out and zipped away.
Under the lid lay a soft cloth, folded flat. It smelled of lamp oil and brass.
Fen shut the lid and tucked the cloth in a pocket. It might help with the lamp.

choices.label: Take the cloth to the tower

passages.title: Gran Tull on the Bench
paragraphs: Gran Tull sat on the bench. She had kept the lamp for many years.
"The lamp is not broken, Fen," she said. "Look at the mirror, not the flame."
Fen did not know what she meant. Fen asked her to tell more.

choices.label: Ask Gran Tull what the mirror can tell you

passages.title: A Small Detail
paragraphs: "Fog is wet air," said Gran Tull. "It leaves wet mist on the brass mirror."
"A misty mirror makes the light dim. Wipe the mirror clean and the lamp will shine."
She pressed a small tin into Fen's hand. "Matches, to light the wick again."
"My knees are slow on stairs. I will stay here on the bench."
Fen smiled. Asking for help had been the right thing to do.

choices.label: Go to the foot of the tower

passages.title: The Foot of the Tower
paragraphs: Fen stood at the tower door. The fog was much too thick, and the shed was hard to see.
Pip sat on the step. Far off, a ship horn gave a low, sad call.
Fen looked at the path and the stairs. Was there more to find first?

choices.label: Go back to the shed and the chest
Go back to the bench and Gran Tull
Climb the stairs to the lamp room

passages.title: The Lamp Room Door
paragraphs: At the top of the stairs, Fen pushed the lamp room door. A gust of wind came in through the open window.
Fen shut the window. The wind must have put out the wick.
The brass mirror stood dull and misty. The wick sat cold in its dish.
Down in the bay, a ship horn called again. Fen took a slow breath and looked at the mirror.

puzzle.prompt: Type the word for the cold string in the dish. It is in the story you just read.
puzzle.hint: It has four letters. It starts with w.
puzzle.successText: Yes, the wick. Fen has the right word for the string that burns.

choices.label: Wipe the mirror and light the wick
choices.lockedHint: You need a cloth from the shed chest, and matches and a clue from Gran Tull.

choices.label: Run down to the dock and wave
Go back down the stairs to look for help

passages.title: The Dark Lamp
paragraphs: Fen rubbed the brass mirror with the cloth. The mist wiped away, and the brass shone.
Then Fen struck a match and lit the wick. A small gold flame woke up and danced.
The mirror caught the flame. A bright beam shot out into the thick fog.
A moth circled the glow and flew off.
The beam must sweep the whole bay. A chain by the mirror turns it.
Fen could pull it alone, or call Gran Tull.

choices.label: Pull the chain and sweep the bay alone
Call Gran Tull to help pull the chain

passages.title: The Bay Shines
paragraphs: Fen pulled the chain, slow and steady. The beam swept over the bay.
One by one, the boats saw the light. Each ship turned toward the harbour.
Soon the dock rang with happy shouts and the smell of fresh fish.
Fen ran down to the bench. Gran Tull gave Fen a hug. "You noticed the small thing," she said.

passages.title: Two Pairs of Hands
paragraphs: Pip had hopped up the stairs behind Fen. Fen called, and Pip flew down to the bench to tap Gran Tull's arm.
Gran Tull looked up. She and Pip climbed the stairs, one slow step at a time. Then she put a hand on the chain.
Together they pulled, and the beam swept the bay twice as fast. The boats saw it at once.
Ship after ship came home, with their fish and happy shouts. Pip snapped at a moth.
Fen sat by the lamp with Pip and Gran Tull. Asking for help had been brave, and it had worked.

passages.title: A Small Light
paragraphs: Fen ran down the path to the dock. The fog was so thick that Fen could not see the water.
Fen waved and waved. A ship horn answered. But no boat came in.
Pip flew to the bench with a loud call. Gran Tull walked down the path and put an arm around Fen.
"Brave try," she said. "The lamp room has the answer."
Fen looked up at the dark tower. Next time, Fen would look at the mirror first, and ask for help.

lighthouse.definition: A tall tower with a big light. It shows ships where the land is.

harbour.definition: A safe place by the sea where boats come to rest.

mirror.definition: A shiny part that bounces light. In the lamp room, it makes the light bright.

window.definition: A hole in a wall with glass in it. It lets in light and air.

answer.definition: What solves a puzzle or a question.

pocket.definition: A small bag sewn into your clothes.

fluttered.definition: Flew with quick, light flaps of the wings.

matches.definition: Thin sticks that make a small flame when you strike them.

match.definition: A thin stick that makes a small flame when you strike it.

wick.definition: The string in a lamp that burns and gives the flame.

gust.definition: A quick puff of strong wind.

stairs.definition: Steps that take you up or down.

knees.definition: The bend in the middle of your leg.
